findings.description: `publish()` saves proofs as posted after `write()` merely logs dry-run GitHub operations, while startup saves `labels-ok` after `ensureLabels()` merely simulates missing-label creation. When `QODO_DRY_RUN=1` uses the default live state, the next real run skips those proofs and trusts the label marker instead of creating missing labels; simulated owner-ask state can also be saved.
findings.title: Dry runs can discard pending PR proofs

findings.description: The dry-run guard in `agent()` executes only after the fresh-ticket setup has fetched Git refs and removed and recreated the ticket worktree. When a ready ticket is selected during rehearsal, the runner can delete an existing worktree at that path despite stopping before the agent runs.
findings.title: A rehearsal can replace a real worktree

findings.description: `publish()` saves `s.posted` only after every proof comment succeeds. If an earlier comment succeeds but a later one fails or the runner stops, the next continuation slices from the old count and creates the successful comments again.
findings.title: Interrupted publishing repeats comments

findings.description: `unpublished()` assumes that a state without `posted` has only its first proof on the PR, although the previous push path commented every later proof too. On an existing run with multiple successfully published proofs, its first continuation reposts all proofs after the first.
findings.title: Older PRs receive duplicate proofs

findings.description: The new retry-limit check throws before `lastAsk` is advanced past the rejected comment. On each later timer tick, the stopped-run scan finds that same comment, reopens the ticket, and posts another stop notification when the check throws again.
findings.title: An extra retry repeatedly stops the run

findings.description: `continueRun()` checks and increments `retryRounds` once for the entire `asks` array, then advances `lastAsk` beyond every comment in it. Several `/agent retry` comments queued before one poll therefore cost a single retry, while retries queued alongside an instruction cost none.
findings.title: Queued retries evade their limit
